svg.title: VAST G1-J8 — signal flow (v2.22.2)
svg.desc: Signal-flow diagram of the VAST G1-J8 web synthesizer: inputs, note and clock processing, sequencers, the synth voice with its oscillators, mixer, filter, VCA, envelopes, LFOs and modulation matrix, the drum machine and sampler channels, the three insert-effect chains, and the master section ending in a stereo output.

g.text: what makes sound, and what plays it
one insert chain per bus · bypassed = disconnected
Every bus has its own chain, in a fixed order, read left to right.
Each effect sits on a dry/wet crossfade; a bypassed effect is disconnected, so it costs nothing.
EQ heads every chain (off by default): it shapes what DIRT drives and what the drum COMP hears.
Only the SYNTH has WAH and SYNTH PAN · only the DRUMS have a COMP · the DRUMS are never ducked.
DUCK listens to no audio: each drum hit schedules its dip at the moment the hit will sound.
DELAY and the FX rates can lock to the tempo (SYNC); DELAY TYPE swaps the whole echo engine.
The synth voice is mono from oscillator to VCA — eight voices sum to one channel.
SPREAD makes it stereo only while a sequencer track is panned off centre.
CHORUS (while on), DELAY in PING PONG and REVERB each add a second channel.
SYNTH PAN always hands the master two channels, so the level never jumps.
Drums and sampler are stereo from each channel's PAN onward.
Single blue line = mono · double blue line = stereo.
TAPE STOP ramps the tempo to 20 BPM and bends the synth down — automation, not an effect.
STUTTER re-maps which step every machine plays; FILL swaps in a drum fill.
The MICROPHONE only reaches the sample studio — it is never monitored.
RENDER TO SAMPLER records the synth after its FX into a sampler slot.
There is no limiter: MASTER COMP is the last dynamics stage.
SCOPE reads the signal before MASTER VOL, so it does not shrink with the volume.
C3–B5 · more octaves on wider screens
Z S X D C V G B H N J M , → C4 – C5
Q 2 W 3 E R 5 T 6 Y 7 U I → C5 – C6
Space play · F fill · Esc panic

g.text: note-on starts both envelopes; the oscillators run
continuously, the VCA opens and closes them
cutoff is a note number, so modulation adds
in semitones; keytrack centres on C4
a voice rests once its tail is below −96 dB
every modulation enters through the MOD BUS
CHOKE: closed hat cuts the open hat

g.text: no FX, no master, not exported
one per voice · mono from oscillator to VCA
CHANNEL ×8 — one per drum track · lane MUTE / SOLO gates the pattern here, never an audition
CHANNEL ×8 — one per slot · lane MUTE / SOLO gates the pattern here, never an audition or a pad
RENDER: the synth after its FX
DRUM HITS — scheduled, no audio sidechain
Every path from a key press to the speakers: notes and clock, the machines, eight synth voices, the drum machine and sampler, three insert chains and the master section.
Read left to right. The colour and line of a wire say what travels on it; a lettered tag (Ⓐ…) continues the wire at the tag with the same letter.
